show: „Na prochach” (Teatr Syrena, Warszawa; polski musical, premiera 2025; reżyseria Robert Talarczyk; scenariusz Jacek Mikołajczyk, Robert Talarczyk, Michał Wybieralski; muzyka Jacek Sotomski i Michał Puchała)
synopsis:
A Konferansjerka brings the Barker family into the spotlight, inviting the audience into a glossy public performance of success: Robert and Rosa Barker, alongside Adam, Archibald and Rupert Barker, present themselves as the architects of a miracle. Their new painkiller promises relief without danger, while Megan Queen, Evelyn Morgan, Oliver Harris, Carole, Becky, Dennis Stone and others pass through a world increasingly shaped by its seductive message. At its centre, Królowa Opioidów enters in long, wordless danced sequences: an alluring, shifting presence who embodies both the drug’s promise and the human cost hidden behind it.

The Barkers turn pain into a market and reassurance into a sales pitch. Their pills circulate ever more widely, but the supposed remedy proves to be opium in tablet form. Dependence spreads from patient to patient, from private suffering into a nationwide catastrophe. What begins as faith in treatment becomes desperation: when access to the pills fails, people move on to heroin bought on the street. Around the family’s polished image, the spectacle darkens, and the roles played by Carole/Konferansjerka/Brenda, Becky/Nancy, and Dennis Stone/dr van Hoff/dr Berkeley/Bob reveal how quickly individual lives can be caught in the machinery of addiction.

As the damage becomes impossible to ignore, the Barkers’ fortune stands against a death toll of more than 500,000 Americans. The reckoning that follows does not restore what has been lost: the makers reach a court settlement that costs them less than they earned, while securing their impunity. The show’s glittering frame turns bitter, exposing how easily wealth, influence and carefully staged language can conceal devastation.

Na prochach is about addiction not merely as an individual affliction, but as a system designed, marketed and protected by power. It confronts the collision of profit and suffering, the seduction of painless solutions, and the unequal consequences of corporate wrongdoing.

show: „Bitwa o tron” (Teatr Syrena, Warszawa; polski musical; muzyka Tomasz Filipczak)
synopsis:
Augustyn Kordecki and Piotr Skarga stride onstage as the hosts of an extravagant televised election show, summoning eight former rulers to compete for the throne of the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth. Henryk Walezy, Stefan Batory, Zygmunt III Waza, Władysław IV Waza, Jan Kazimierz Waza, Jan III Sobieski, August II Mocny and Stanisław August Poniatowski must each turn a reign into a crowd-winning musical number, promising glory, influence and—repeatedly—the recovery of Inflanty. Their contest replaces solemn portrait-gallery history with celebrity spectacle: monarchs sell their achievements, expose their vanities and fight to be remembered as the ruler Poland most needs.

Henryk Walezy opens with unabashed ambition, while the formidable Stefan Batory makes a flamboyantly predatory entrance. Zygmunt III Waza promotes himself as the country’s coolest king; Władysław IV resists being defined by another person’s desires and expectations; and Jan Kazimierz confronts the cycles of collapse and recovery that marked his troubled rule. Jan III Sobieski’s public image is complicated and softened by his devotion to Maria Kazimiera, while August II Mocny revels in his divided identity and outsized power. Finally, Stanisław August Poniatowski looks back in pain and self-reproach as the Commonwealth approaches its partition and disappearance.

Bona Sforza, Anna Wazówna, Maria Kazimiera and Katarzyna Wielka form the judging panel. They interrupt the kings’ self-congratulation to insist that women—mothers, sisters, wives, lovers and rulers—also shaped the country’s history, and they call for a “new gallery” in which those figures are no longer relegated to the margins. When every contestant has made his appeal, the audience itself casts the decisive vote, so the winner’s coronation changes from performance to performance.

The musical treats national history as a contest over memory: who gets celebrated, who is blamed, and who is allowed to speak. Beneath its comic talent-show format, it questions heroic mythmaking, masculine power and the gap between a ruler’s polished image and the consequences of rule.

show: „Starzyński” (Teatr Syrena, Warszawa; autorska premiera musicalowa Teatru Syrena)
synopsis:
Stefan Starzyński sits alone at his desk in Warsaw’s ratusz, listening to a numbing roar in his ears as evening falls on 26 October 1939. The city outside has been defeated and damaged by war; its inhabitants face German occupation, and the mayor, now living in the building from which he once governed, is exhausted by helplessness, guilt and grief. Visitors still cross the threshold—a secretary, petitioners and Stanisław Lorentz, his trusted colleague, friend and director of the Muzeum Narodowe—but their practical concerns cannot quiet the questions consuming him. Should he resist an occupier who holds all the power, cooperate to spare civilians further suffering, or preserve his own life when Warsaw itself seems beyond saving?

As the night deepens, the ratusz becomes the landscape of Starzyński’s mind. Memories, dreams and hallucinations crowd into the room, blurring the boundary between the present and the past. His mother and father appear; Syrena enters as an embodiment of the city; Józef Piłsudski returns as a commanding figure from political memory; and Ludwika Nitschowa, who will one day create Starzyński’s monument, confronts the living man with the image posterity will make of him. Echoes of Adam Mickiewicz’s Dziady intensify the pull between sacrifice, revolt and survival, while the physical space around Starzyński increasingly yields to the logic of his visions.

Morning on 27 October offers no true resolution. Starzyński joins a crowd in voicing the promise that Warsaw will be rebuilt, only to be arrested by the Germans. As he is taken away, the man disappears from the ruined ratusz, leaving behind his fears, memories, visions and the outline of a future monument.

The musical examines how an introverted administrator is pressed by catastrophe into becoming a public symbol of resistance. It asks whether heroism is a chosen act or a role forced upon someone by history, and sets private despair against Warsaw’s enduring hope of renewal.

show: „Kajko i Kokosz. Szkoła latania” (Teatr Syrena, Warszawa; musicalowa adaptacja komiksu Janusza Christy)
synopsis:
Night falls as Mirmił returns from a hunt with his most trusted warriors, Kajko and Kokosz, only to find the gates of Mirmiłowo shut against them. Forced to spend the night outside, the three wander into a succession of mishaps: Łamignat mistakes them for enemies while testing a magical flute given to him by his wife, Jaga, and Krwawy Hegemon’s Zbójcerze seize the chance to attack. When the travellers finally regain the gród at dawn, an indignant Mirmił orders that its gates must never again be closed. Hegemon promptly turns that decree to his advantage. His men slip inside in disguise, sowing disorder among the inhabitants and attacking Mirmił’s home, but Kajko, Kokosz, and the people of Mirmiłowo drive them out.

Humiliated, Hegemon adopts a subtler strategy. He fills the kasztelan’s mind with visions of flight, knowing that Mirmił’s new obsession can remove him from the gród. Mirmił first seeks Jaga’s help and attempts to fly on a broomstick, with spectacularly painful results that leave both him and the witch’s household worse for wear. Hegemon then points him toward the Wyższa Szkoła Latania na Miotle on Łysa Góra. Despite Lubawa’s objections, Mirmił sets out with Kajko and Kokosz, endures further comic obstacles on the road, and earns a diploma, flying ointment, and a flying trunk.

While the three are away, Hegemon launches his planned assault on Mirmiłowo. Łamignat, Jaga, and the townspeople withstand the first attack; then Mirmił, Kajko, and Kokosz return in time to join the defence. Their improvised airborne counterattack routs the Zbójcerze, and the grateful community celebrates Mirmił as Mirmił Waleczny.

The musical turns a desire for personal glory into a test of responsibility: Mirmił must learn that leadership cannot be abandoned for fantasy. Its comic adventures also celebrate loyalty, communal courage, and resourcefulness in the face of manipulation and invasion.

show: „Wypiór” (Teatr Syrena, Warszawa; spektakl na podstawie powieści Grzegorza Uzdańskiego; adaptacja i reżyseria Jacek Jabrzyk; muzyka Mariusz Obijalski)
synopsis:
Marta and Łukasz are trying to survive a crisis in their relationship when the presence in their Warsaw flat begins to demand attention. By daylight, Adam Mickiewicz—now a vampire—lies concealed in the wardrobe, shielding himself from the lethal sun; after dark, he slips out into the city, sustaining himself on blood taken from a hospital bin. The great Romantic poet has not vanished into a monument or a schoolbook. He is a needy, unruly, disturbingly tangible third presence in the lives of two contemporary thirty-somethings.

Their home stands near pl. Zbawiciela, in the fashionable centre of Warsaw, where ordinary pressures of adulthood already test Marta and Łukasz’s attachment to one another. Mickiewicz’s nocturnal existence turns that domestic strain into an increasingly surreal encounter between present-day urban life and the afterlife of Polish Romanticism. His hunger, his habits, and his formidable cultural baggage intrude on the couple’s private world, while the city around them becomes a terrain in which the vampire-poet may be encountered, pursued, remembered, or reinvented.

As the action moves through a shifting gallery of figures—including Syrenka, Pielęgniarka, Zofia Szymanowska, prof. Klicka, Matka, Detektyw, Stróż, Dyrektor muzeum, and Kot Eks—Marta and Łukasz must confront more than an impossible housemate. Mickiewicz carries with him a language of grand feeling, national myth, love, sacrifice, and poetic destiny: values that can seem absurdly disproportionate to a modern relationship under pressure, yet cannot simply be dismissed. The question is not merely whether the vampire will make their shared life unbearable, but whether a figure so burdened by history and romance can still offer the couple a way back to each other.

The show turns a relationship crisis into a collision between contemporary Warsaw and the lingering force of Romantic imagination. Its themes include love under strain, cultural memory, the uneasy inheritance of national icons, and the possibility that old ideals may still help save an intimate life.

show: „Mistrz i Małgorzata” (Teatr Studio Buffo, Warszawa; muzyka Janusz Stokłosa; libretto Galina Polidi i Yury Ryashentsev; reżyseria Janusz Józefowicz)
synopsis:
Woland arrives in Moscow with his uncanny retinue—Korowiow, Behemot, Azazello and Hella—and turns a city gripped by Stalinist fear into the setting for a sequence of ruthless, grotesque revelations. In a world already ruled by cruelty, the visitors need hardly create evil themselves: they merely expose the greed, cowardice and hypocrisy concealed beneath official certainty. Their disturbances draw in Iwan Bezdomny, whose encounter with the supernatural sends him in search of an explanation for events that defy the city’s materialist logic.

Elsewhere, the Mistrz has written a novel that summons an ancient Jerusalem ruled by Piłat. There Jeszua faces authority, betrayal and death, while Piłat is left burdened by a moral failure he cannot undo. The Mistrz’s artistic act—his insistence on depicting uncompromising goodness amid terror—brings persecution rather than recognition. Broken by the forces around him, he disappears from Małgorzata’s life.

Refusing to abandon him, Małgorzata accepts Azazello’s invitation and undergoes a transformation into a witch. She crosses into Woland’s fantastic domain and becomes hostess of the Bal Pełni Księżyca, where the dead and the damned assemble before Satan. Her ordeal is not undertaken for power or revenge but for the chance to find the Mistrz again. When that chance comes, Małgorzata’s steadfast love secures their reunion. Together they leave the oppressive reality that has destroyed their earthly refuge and enter a “piąty wymiar,” a mysterious realm that offers them sanctuary.

The musical sets love and artistic freedom against an environment in which fear corrupts both public life and private conscience. Its intertwining worlds ask whether mercy, moral courage and imagination can survive when evil has become ordinary.

show: „Romeo i Julia” (Teatr Studio Buffo, Warszawa; muzyka Janusz Stokłosa; polski tekst Agata Miklaszewska; reżyseria i choreografia Janusz Józefowicz) — NIE francuski musical „Roméo et Juliette”
synopsis:
Julia is swept into the glare and noise of a commercial adult world where her parents, Pani Capuletti and Pan Capuletti, are too absorbed in their own battles to hear what she wants. Their plans point her toward Parys, the approved and advantageous match, while Niania tries to protect Julia within the limits of a household ruled by pressure, image and money. Yet Julia’s meeting with Romeo opens a private space of tenderness and defiance: two young people discover a love that refuses to be negotiated by their elders.

Around them, desire and danger race through the city. Romeo’s recent attachment to Rosalina lingers in the background, while Benvolio and Merkucjo pull him into a volatile world of friendship, bravado and confrontation. Tybalt becomes the sharpest expression of the adults’ hostility and the violence surrounding Julia’s family. When conflict erupts, the consequences are fatal: killing turns youthful rivalry into grief, and the possibility of a future for Julia and Romeo narrows with every attempt to control them.

The threat is not only family authority. Dealer draws the young people into a drug-fuelled undercurrent that intensifies their vulnerability and makes escape feel both tempting and destructive. As the lovers turn to Ojciec Laurenty for help, they seek a path beyond the demands imposed on them. But secrecy, fear and mistrust replace honest conversation. The adults press forward with their arrangements, the young people take increasingly desperate risks, and the lovers’ hope culminates in suicide, leaving mourning where reconciliation might have been.

At its heart, the musical sets uncompromising young love against a ruthless, commercialised adult world. It is a tragedy of parents and children unable to talk, listen or respect one another’s needs—and of what is lost when power, profit, drugs and violence drown out compassion.

show: „Piotruś Pan” (Teatr Studio Buffo, Warszawa; libretto i teksty Jeremi Przybora; muzyka Janusz Stokłosa; reżyseria Janusz Józefowicz; prapremiera 2000 w Teatrze Muzycznym Roma)
synopsis:
Piotruś Pan slips into the Darling children’s bedroom one night, where Wendy, Jaś and Miś are under the watchful care of Nana. His irrepressible invitation to fly carries the three children away from Pan Darling and Pani Darling, across the night sky and into a remote, fantastic world of peril, play and perpetual childhood.

There they encounter Piotruś’s unruly companions—Powtórka, Ciutek, Trąbal, Rybol and Szpic—as well as Tygrysica z Lilią w Zębach and her father, Wódz Olbrzymia Pantera Mniejsza. Yet adventure is shadowed by danger. Kapitan Hak and his pirates, including Sznaps, pursue Piotruś with cultivated fury: this supposedly refined pirate cannot bear Piotruś’s insolent manner, while a crocodile remains an ever-present threat. The children are drawn into the conflict as pirate schemes divide the group and force them to discover courage, loyalty and resourcefulness.

Wendy increasingly takes on the role of protector and comforter among the boys. Her tenderness creates an emotional bond with Piotruś, who enjoys being admired but resists every suggestion that he exchange freedom for ordinary family life. In the climactic confrontation, the children and their allies face Hak’s crew, and the immediate danger is overcome. But the greater question remains: whether the pleasures of never growing up can replace a home, parents and the passage of time.

Wendy, Jaś and Miś ultimately choose to return to the Darling household, while Piotruś stays behind. Years later, he comes back to find Dorosła Wendy and meets Jane, Wendy’s daughter, opening the possibility that another child may answer his call to adventure.

The musical contrasts the exhilaration of imagination and independence with the sustaining force of family, care and belonging. Its central feeling is bittersweet: childhood can be revisited through memory and play, but it cannot remain unchanged forever.

show: „A Pál utcai fiúk” (Vígszínház, Budapest; zene Dés László, dalszöveg Geszti Péter, színpadi változat Grecsó Krisztián, rendező Marton László)
synopsis:
Boka and the boys of Pál utca claim the Grund as their own small republic: a dusty vacant lot where they build forts, play battles and defend their hard-won freedom. Their order is formal but affectionate—Boka is their respected leader, while the smallest member, Nemecsek, holds the humblest rank and nevertheless longs to prove that he belongs. When the Pásztor brothers humiliate Nemecsek and seize the boys’ treasured golyók, the insult becomes a warning: Áts Feri and the red-shirted boys from the Füvészkert intend to take the Grund.

Boka prepares the defence, but the group is weakened from within. Geréb, jealous of Boka’s authority and tempted by Áts Feri’s promise of importance, secretly bargains with the enemy. Nemecsek discovers the treachery and ventures into the Füvészkert to expose it. He is caught, thrown into the cold water, and returns ill—yet he refuses to abandon the cause. Even when the Gittegylet unjustly doubts him and threatens to punish him, Nemecsek’s loyalty does not waver. Geréb, confronted by the consequences of his betrayal and by Nemecsek’s courage, seeks forgiveness and is allowed back among the boys.

The red shirts finally attack. In the fight for the Grund, Nemecsek, feverish and physically exhausted, reappears to help turn the battle. The Pál utcai boys prevail, and Áts Feri acknowledges the bravery of the frail boy he had underestimated. But Nemecsek’s illness worsens after his sacrifice; Boka and the others must face the devastating fact that their victory cannot save their friend. Soon afterward, the boys learn that the Grund itself is to be built over, ending the world they fought to protect.

The musical makes childhood play into a struggle for dignity, loyalty and a place to belong. It asks what courage costs, how betrayal can be redeemed, and why even the most cherished territory may prove temporary.

show: „Két összeillő ember” (Déryné Társulat; szerző Csikós Attila; rendező Tarsoly Krisztina)
synopsis:
Szécsi Pál stands after Domján Edit’s death and lets memory pull him back to the ten months that bound them together: a brief, fierce affair between two celebrated artists who seem to recognise the loneliness beneath each other’s brilliance. Their meeting at Magyar Rádió in 1972 ignites a relationship of exhilarating intimacy and abrupt collision. Domján Edit, already a renowned actress, has fought her way out of poverty and built a career admired by audiences, yet carries a persistent dread of ageing, abandonment, and death. Szécsi Pál, the adored singer whose charm and voice have made him a public idol, remains inwardly the frightened child marked by abandonment, foster homes, and state care.

As their love deepens, each hopes the other can supply the safety life has denied them. Domján Edit tries to give Szécsi Pál steadiness and a home; he seeks in her both a lover and the unconditional protection he has never stopped craving. But affection cannot dissolve the wounds they bring into the relationship. Their temperaments flare, reconciliation follows quarrel, and their happiness repeatedly gives way to misunderstanding. Although they want to live together, they speak past one another, caught between their need for closeness and their terror of being hurt.

Szécsi Pál’s dependence on alcohol and medication increasingly erodes the possibility of rescue. Domján Edit struggles to keep him alive, but he resists the help offered to him. The framing memory makes clear that their separation does not end their hold on one another: Szécsi Pál recalls love, blame, tenderness, and loss after Domján Edit has taken her own life, while his own self-destruction waits beyond the remembered months.

The musical portrays fame as a fragile public light that cannot cure private despair. It is a tragedy of two gifted people whose love is genuine, yet proves too burdened by childhood wounds, addiction, loneliness, and the inability to accept salvation.

show: „A kör” EDDA musical (Várudvari Nyári Színház és kaposvári Csiky Gergely Színház koprodukció; szövegkönyv Oravecz János; zeneszerző Gömöry Zsolt; rendező Gémes Antos)
synopsis:
A soul in heaven chooses the life awaiting it as Elmó’s son, speaking with az Univerzum before the story descends to a world of love, ambition, music and political unrest. Elmó grows up with a restless desire to find his place, caught between the pull of romance, the promise of success and the loyalty demanded by the people around him.

His relationship with Angóra cannot withstand the divisions between them. Though Elmó loves her, Angóra sees the match as beneath her and leaves him, shaped in part by the influence of her powerful father, Fausztusz. As Fausztusz pursues the presidency, his public campaign becomes a looming force in Elmó’s life. Meanwhile, Elmó is drawn into the orbit of Szezár, the formidable leader of a motorcycle gang, and meets Szezár’s sister, Írisz. Their connection offers Elmó a more honest, hard-won possibility of love and belonging.

Frédi recognizes Elmó’s talent and becomes his manager, steering him towards a career as a successful singer. Yet professional triumph cannot insulate Elmó and his friends from the country’s worsening tensions. When Fausztusz wins the election, he addresses a huge celebratory rally and admits that his campaign has not been entirely truthful: austerity is coming. The revelation ignites an uprising. In the violence that follows, Frédi is shot, and darkness falls over the stage.

Ten years later, Elmó and Írisz have built a life together and have a son. The final image returns to Frédi’s earlier vision of the child before his birth, joining loss, memory and renewal across generations.

The musical treats adulthood as a series of choices between love, money, fame, loyalty and power. Its central movement is circular: lives begin with hope, are scarred by betrayal and upheaval, and nevertheless continue through family, music and the possibility of a different future.

show: 音樂劇《天堂邊緣》(2004 年兩廳院「中文音樂劇實驗計畫」原創作品;編劇暨作詞 王友輝、作曲 冉天豪)
synopsis:
秀燕、何智 and 菲菲 have remained at 震宇’s side from the moment he was born, three souls adrift in the human world and unable to move on. For twenty-nine years, they have watched over him, sharing the invisible proximity of his life while remaining bound to the world they have not been able to leave. Their long, unexplained vigil is abruptly interrupted when 天使 appears with a condition: before they can begin their journey to heaven, each of the three must resolve a final regret within twenty-four hours.

With time closing in, the spirits and 震宇 are drawn into an urgent search through the ties that shape a life. The task leads them across the fragile terrain of family love, friendship and romantic love, where old absences, unspoken feelings and unfinished connections cannot simply be set aside. As the deadline approaches, the question is not merely whether the three souls can depart, but what it means to face the things that have continued to hold them here. Their pursuit turns the ordinary human bonds surrounding 震宇 into a passage between the living and the dead, asking each person to confront attachment, courage and the possibility of release. The journey is at once comic, tender and increasingly poignant, as a single day becomes an opportunity to acknowledge what was lost and what still deserves to be cherished.

True fulfilment, the musical suggests, does not come from living without regrets. It comes from learning to let go and from recognising the value of everyone who remains close to us.

show: 『カラフルランウェイ！プリキュア』The Stage(2026年12月 天王洲銀河劇場・COOL JAPAN PARK OSAKA;原作 東堂いづみ;脚本・演出 ほさかよう;音楽 藤田淳平)
synopsis:
Kamishiro Ayato, Hachibari Itsuki, Mikuriya Oji, and Envy step into ordinary days shaped by friendship, personal style, and the pressure to express who they truly are. Yet when trouble threatens the colour and confidence that fashion gives to people’s lives, the four young men transform into Cure Silhouette, Cure Collage, Cure Flash, and Cure Trad: a new team of Precure whose powers shine in the distinct visual language each one chooses to wear.

As the group faces an adversarial presence embodied by Bogart, Banshee, and Gothic, the boys must confront more than spectacular danger. Each is tested by insecurity, clashing tastes, and the fear that standing out will leave him isolated. Ayato’s sensitivity to form and outline, Itsuki’s instinct for assembling unlikely elements, Oji’s drive to make a brilliant impression, and Envy’s respect for enduring style initially pull them in different directions. Their work alongside Momose Akihiko makes clear that neither fashionable clothes nor heroic identities can simply be copied from someone else: both must be made one’s own.

Battles become vivid displays of song, action, transformation, and runway-like self-presentation. The four Cures learn to turn their differences into a shared strength, creating combinations no single vision could achieve. As the enemies seek to distort individuality into conformity or empty appearance, the team fights to protect the freedom to choose, change, and be seen as oneself.

At its heart, the story celebrates fashion as a language of identity rather than a matter of surface alone. It argues that courage grows when people honour their own colours while making room for the colours of others.

show: 忍劇「NARUTO-ナルト-」(2027年2月〜 京都・南座;原作 岸本斉史;演出 植木豪;構成 亀田真二郎)
synopsis:
Naruto Uzumaki, a lonely and reckless young ninja of Konohagakure, refuses to let the fear and suspicion surrounding him decide his future. Determined to earn recognition and one day become Hokage, he enters the Ninja Academy’s ranks alongside the gifted, brooding Sasuke Uchiha and the sharp-minded Sakura Haruno. Under the guidance of their newly appointed teacher, Kakashi Hatake, the three are forced to confront a difficult truth: talent alone cannot make them a team. Rivalry, impatience, and personal ambition repeatedly threaten to divide them, yet demanding training and perilous missions teach them to rely on one another. Naruto’s stubborn optimism challenges Sasuke’s isolation and Sakura’s uncertainty, while Kakashi tests whether his students can place comrades above individual success. As their world exposes them to danger beyond the classroom, Naruto must prove that the outcast everyone dismisses possesses not only extraordinary resolve, but also the power to inspire those fighting beside him. His journey turns every failure into another chance to grow, transforming the bonds of Team 7 into a source of courage against fear, loneliness, and despair. The official production identifies its story as Naruto’s boyhood arc in Konohagakure, centred on his growth alongside his companions.

At its heart, the story concerns belonging: Naruto seeks recognition, while Sasuke, Sakura, and Kakashi each learn what it means to trust others. It also celebrates perseverance, friendship, and the choice to protect one’s comrades even when personal wounds and rivalries make that choice difficult.

show: „Caperucita Roja, El Musical” (Teatro Telón de Asfalto, Ciudad de México)
synopsis:
Caperucita Roja steps into the forest carrying a basket of food for la abuelita, her curiosity drawing her toward every sound and shadow along the way. Brave and full of energy, she is determined to complete her errand, but the woods hold dangers that demand more caution than she expects.

Watching her closely is the Lobo Feroz. Cunning and hungry, he forms a scheme to get to la abuelita’s house before Caperucita Roja does, intending to eat them both. As his plan unfolds, Caperucita Roja must navigate the forest while confronting the consequences of trusting too readily and straying from the guidance she has been given. The threat of the Lobo Feroz turns an ordinary visit into a lively adventure shaped by comic mishaps, suspenseful encounters, action, and music.

Caperucita Roja is not left to face the danger alone. With the support of her friends and an unexpected hero, she finds the help she needs when the Lobo Feroz’s scheme puts la abuelita and herself at risk. Their intervention changes the course of the journey and gives Caperucita Roja the chance to act with the courage she already possesses, now tempered by greater care. Rather than simply rushing ahead, she begins to understand why listening to older people’s advice matters—and why attentiveness can be as important as bravery.

The story celebrates friendship, courage, and the importance of looking out for one another. Through comedy, action, and songs for the whole family, it also presents a gentle lesson about listening to elders, recognising danger, and making wiser choices.

show: „Germans de sang” / Blood Brothers (Teatre Condal, Barcelona; versió catalana; llibret, música i lletres Willy Russell; adaptació al català Albert Mas-Griera; direcció Daniel Anglès)
synopsis:
Mrs Johnstone, abandoned by her husband and struggling to feed her large family, gives birth to twin boys just as Mrs Lyons, her wealthy but childless employer, longs for a baby of her own. Desperate for security, Mrs Johnstone agrees to give one newborn to Mrs Lyons, who raises him as Eddie while the other remains Mickey Johnstone. Horrified by the bargain’s moral weight, Mrs Lyons invokes a superstition: if the twins ever learn they are brothers, both will die. The secret divides the boys between sharply unequal worlds—Mickey amid poverty, overcrowding and hardship, Eddie amid privilege, education and expectation.

Yet chance repeatedly draws them together. As children, Mickey and Eddie meet, instantly become inseparable, and swear themselves “blood brothers,” unaware that their bond is literal. Mrs Johnstone moves her family away to prevent further contact, while Mrs Lyons becomes increasingly fearful that Eddie will discover the truth. Years later, the two young men reunite; Mickey’s close friend Linda joins them, and the affection among the three grows increasingly complicated.

Adulthood exposes how profoundly class has shaped their prospects. Eddie advances toward a secure public life, while Mickey’s life is narrowed by unemployment, despair and the consequences of Sammy’s criminal violence. Mickey and Linda marry, but financial pressure, prison and medication leave him emotionally shattered. When Eddie offers practical support to Linda and her child, Mickey—misled into believing that Eddie has taken Linda as well as every opportunity he lacked—turns on his brother. Mrs Johnstone finally reveals their shared birth, but the revelation comes too late: Mickey shoots Eddie, and the police kill Mickey.

The musical confronts the cruelty of class inequality and asks whether identity is made by birth, upbringing or social circumstance. It also turns secrecy, maternal sacrifice and superstition into a tragic warning: love cannot protect people forever from the systems and choices that have shaped their lives.

show: „On Your Feet!” (the Emilio and Gloria Estefan musical; The Argyle Theatre at Babylon Village production)
synopsis:
Gloria Estefan steps offstage during a 1990 concert to find Emilio Estefan and their son, Nayib, waiting backstage, and the moment opens into memories of the road that brought them there. As a young Cuban immigrant in Miami, Gloria pours her feelings into songs while coping with her father José Fajardo’s absence during the Vietnam War and her mother Gloria Fajardo’s insistence that music cannot provide a secure future. Her grandmother, Consuelo, recognizes the strength of Gloria’s voice and urges her not to silence it. When Emilio, the driven leader of the Miami Latin Boys, hears Gloria sing, he invites her to rehearse with the band. Their professional partnership soon becomes a romance, though Gloria’s mother distrusts Emilio and fears that her daughter will inherit the disappointments she herself has endured.

Gloria and Emilio reshape the group into the Miami Sound Machine, performing relentlessly at small engagements and fighting record executives who believe their Spanish-language sound cannot cross into the American mainstream. Emilio presses for English-language recordings while Gloria insists on retaining the rhythm, identity, and energy of their music. Their persistence leads to hit records, international touring, marriage, and the birth of Nayib, but success also brings exhaustion and deepens the rift between Gloria and her mother. When Emilio persuades an overworked Gloria to add one more date in Syracuse, their tour bus is struck by a truck during a snowstorm. Gloria suffers a devastating spinal injury and faces emergency surgery, haunted by the possibility that she may never walk again. Supported by Emilio, reconciled with her mother, and sustained by memories of José and Consuelo, she endures rehabilitation and ultimately returns to the stage in triumph.

The musical celebrates artistic conviction, family loyalty, and the determination to preserve one’s cultural voice while reaching a wider world. It also frames love not as an escape from hardship, but as the force that helps Gloria and Emilio confront loss, ambition, fear, and recovery together.

show: „Carrie: The Musical” (book Lawrence D. Cohen, music Michael Gore, lyrics Dean Pitchford; Bay Street Players / State Theatre, Eustis, Florida production)
synopsis:
A terrified Carrie White stands in the girls’ locker room as her first period begins, only to be met with the laughter and cruelty of classmates led by Chris Hargensen. The humiliation awakens a force Carrie has scarcely understood: objects move when her fear and anger rise. Miss Gardner stops the abuse and punishes the girls, while Carrie returns to the restrictive home ruled by her mother, Margaret White. Margaret interprets every ordinary sign of growing up as sin, warning Carrie that the world outside is corrupt and that her daughter must be saved from it.

At school, Sue Snell is shaken by her part in the locker-room cruelty. Wanting to make amends, she persuades her boyfriend, Tommy Ross, to invite Carrie to the prom in Sue’s place. Carrie initially believes the invitation is another trap, and Margaret fiercely forbids her to go, but Tommy’s gentleness and Miss Gardner’s encouragement allow Carrie to imagine, for once, being accepted. She makes a dress, defies her mother, and arrives at the prom transformed by hope.

Chris, excluded from the event because of her bullying, refuses to let Carrie have that happiness. With her boyfriend, Billy Nolan, she prepares a vicious revenge: a bucket of pig’s blood positioned above the stage. When Carrie and Tommy are named prom king and queen, the applause briefly gives Carrie the belonging she has long desired. Then the blood falls. Convinced that everyone is laughing at her again, Carrie’s powers erupt. The celebration becomes catastrophe as she turns her rage on the school and those inside it.

Carrie returns home wounded and shattered, seeking comfort from Margaret. Instead, Margaret treats her as a monstrous sinner and attacks her. Carrie uses her power to stop her mother, but she cannot escape the devastation surrounding her or within herself.

The musical examines how cruelty, isolation, and religious repression can turn longing for acceptance into destructive fury. It also asks whether remorse and kindness can matter when they arrive after irreversible harm has already been done.

show: „A Charlie Brown Christmas: Live on Stage” (touring stage production adapted from Charles M. Schulz; music by Vince Guaraldi)
synopsis:
Snow falls as Charlie Brown joins Linus, Snoopy, Lucy, Sally, Schroeder, Patty, Violet, Frieda and the other children in the pleasures of Christmas time, yet he cannot share their excitement. The season leaves him strangely sad: no Christmas cards arrive for him, and the cheerful rituals around him seem hollow. At Lucy’s psychiatric booth, he pays five cents for advice. After deciding that he suffers from “pantaphobia,” a fear of everything, Lucy gives him a practical cure: he should direct the neighborhood Christmas play.

Charlie Brown accepts, hoping that responsibility will make the holiday feel meaningful. Instead, commercial excess seems to meet him at every turn. Snoopy turns his doghouse into an extravagant entry for the neighborhood lights-and-display contest, while Sally asks Charlie Brown to compose an ambitious letter to Santa Claus. Rehearsal is equally discouraging. The cast prefers lively dancing, noisy music and Lucy’s grand vision of a “Christmas Queen” to the quiet, sincere play Charlie Brown imagines. Unable to create the right mood, he decides the production needs a real Christmas tree.

Lucy recommends a large pink aluminum tree, but Charlie Brown and Linus find a small, bare sapling instead. Charlie Brown chooses it because he believes it only needs care to become beautiful. When he brings it back, the other children ridicule both him and the fragile tree. Hurt and overwhelmed, he asks whether anyone truly knows what Christmas is about. Linus steps forward and gives the answer that changes the room. Renewed, Charlie Brown takes the little tree away to decorate it himself, but a single heavy ornament makes it droop, and he believes he has ruined it. The others soon recognize their unkindness, restore the tree together, and welcome Charlie Brown back with a joyful Christmas song.

The story contrasts spectacle, competition and gift-getting with simplicity, generosity and shared understanding. Its heart lies in Charlie Brown’s need to be seen and in his friends’ eventual choice to turn regret into care, community and celebration.
